annotation.title_clean: The Future of Sex Robots in Indonesia: Law, Science, and Technology
annotation.title_en: The Future of Sex Robots in Indonesia: Law, Science, and Technology
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Taqwa, M.D.; Alfarizy, A.; Sirait, M.Y.L.
annotation.venue: Jurnal IUS Kajian Hukum dan Keadilan
annotation.summary_en: Normative-hypothetical legal analysis of sex robots in Indonesia, combining science and technology description with Indonesian law. It weighs arguments for (economic, psychological, no harm to others) and against (religion, decency, objectification), concluding that individual use can still be prohibited if it violates law, morals or public interest.
key_provisions_or_claims: Sex robots are not freely sold in Indonesia, and no prior Indonesian legal study exists.
Individual private use does not preclude prohibition if it violates law, moral values or public interest.
Proponents cite economic benefit, psychological benefit and absence of harm to others.
Opponents cite religious values, decency and sexual objectification of women.
Argument that robots could replace prostitution is rejected; the normative solution is banning prostitution.
